items.title: 19.3.1 Models Proposed for the Mechanism of DNA Replication

source_refs.note: Topic 19.3.1 (PDF 123); Figure 19.8 is replaced by the original diagram.

blocks.text: Three models were proposed for the basic mechanism of DNA replication.

1- Conservative model: According to this model, the double-helix of parent DNA remains intact. This double-helix generates new double-helix which completely consists of new material. So, after replication, when two daughter DNAs are produced;

items: 1 daughter DNA contains both strands of parent DNA, and
1 daughter DNA contains both new strands.

blocks.text: 2- Semi-conservative model: According to this model, the double-helix of parent DNA is broken. It means that two strands of parent DNA separate. Each of these strands acts as a template for the synthesis of a new strand. So, after replication;

items: Both daughter DNAs consist of one strand of parent DNA and one new strand.

blocks.text: 3- Dispersive model: According to this model, parent double-helix DNA is broken and dispersed into nucleotides. Then, each nucleotide combines with new nucleotides to generate the four strands of daughter DNAs. So, after replication;

items: Both daughter DNAs contain strands which are mixtures of old and new nucleotides.

blocks.alt: Three panels, one replication round each. In every panel a parental DNA double helix (both strands red, old) undergoes replication into two daughter DNAs. 1- Conservative model: one daughter is all new (blue) and one all old (red). 2- Semi-conservative model: each daughter has one old and one new strand. 3- Dispersive model: each strand of both daughters is a mix of old and new pieces.
